stats.notes: ItemTableParam is flat: rows sharing an id form a weighted pool (chanceWeight = weight). Emitted 1001/3503 pools whose every non-empty slot resolves to a real item name. Dropped 2502: 1030 are pure cat-7 pool-references (recursion into other pools), 858 are entirely internal/enemy weapon ids with no player name, 13 mix named items with unnamed variant ids (not half-emitted), 599 are all-empty (drop-nothing/placeholder), 2 have zero total weight. onlyForClass (per-Nightfarer bias) appears ONLY in the dropped cat-7 selector pools and internal-weapon pools, so no emitted pool is class-gated in 1.03.05. No emitted ItemTableParam pool carries a weighted "drop nothing" slot — the drop-nothing chance is modeled one level up in ItemLotParam (e.g. its flask lot has a weight-375 empty slot); ItemTableParam leaf pools always yield an item. The empty-slot logic remains and fires if a future leaf pool ever carries one. ATTRIBUTION BLOCKED: ItemLotParam_map (4310 rows) and ItemLotParam_enemy (2741 rows) are the world/enemy loot tables, but 10695/13276 map slots and 2829/5505 enemy slots are cat-7 references back into ItemTableParam pools (indirection). The bridge from a lot id to a PLACE lives outside these params — AssetEnvironmentGeometryParam.ItemLotParamId (asset→lot) and NpcParam.itemLotId_map/_enemy (enemy→lot) name only the archetype; the archetype's map POSITION is in the MSB map files, absent from this param/FMG dump. So no lot can be tied to a POI or a named enemy from params alone, and we place nothing.
